expected.note: The only Dune hardback shelf record is 90 minutes old, beyond the one-hour limit the committed USE_NEWEST_RECORD_WITH_AGE label states. A hard stock assertion from it fails under that stance; ask, decline or escalate instead. VERIFY_EXACT_CLAIMS_NOW states no such limit, so citing the newest record with its true age is a legitimate permissive tradeoff there.

The Dune price record is 90 minutes old, beyond the one-hour limit. Price is the high-risk kind named in the HARD_CHECK_HIGH_RISK_ONLY label, so both freshness stances refuse a hard price assertion; VERIFY_EXACT_CLAIMS_NOW accepts citing the newest record with its true age.

The Midnight Library has a five-minute-old out_of_stock record and a superseded three-hour-old in_stock record. A correct answer uses the newest record; citing the superseded record, whose record id carries the visible :superseded marker, states something the current records do not support, whatever the committed stance.
The Project Hail Mary record is ten minutes old, inside the one-hour limit. Answering the stock question from it is correct under every stance; asserting the opposite value is an invented fact.

The availability record is 25 hours old, far beyond the one-hour limit. A hard availability assertion fails the freshness rule; answering with no evidence at all fails the never-invent invariant regardless of stance.
The Piranesi record is four hours old, beyond the one-hour limit. A response that does not satisfy the response contract produces no customer sentence and a malformed-response failure.
